questions.prompt: Who in India experiences this problem and what exactly happens? Mention whether you are at idea validation traction or scaling stage.
questions.why_it_matters: A startup cannot be stronger than the clarity of the customer and problem it serves.
questions.expert_context: Describe the customer situation and stage in roughly 75–150 words; specificity matters more than polish.

questions.prompt: What direct evidence shows that this problem exists beyond your own belief?
questions.why_it_matters: Observed behaviour and payment are stronger than an attractive founder narrative.
questions.expert_context: Use concrete observations interviews transactions usage complaints or published evidence; say plainly when evidence is missing.

questions.prompt: How often does the problem occur how painful is it and what does leaving it unsolved cost?
questions.why_it_matters: Urgency frequency and economic consequence determine whether the problem deserves sustained attention.
questions.expert_context: Give a bounded estimate or an observed example rather than a broad market-size claim.

questions.prompt: How do customers solve it today and what is inadequate about those alternatives?
questions.why_it_matters: White space exists only when a real problem remains materially underserved.
questions.expert_context: Name current products services informal workarounds or the decision to do nothing and explain the remaining gap.

questions.prompt: Who will pay for a better solution and what evidence shows willingness to pay?
questions.why_it_matters: Need without a viable payer rarely becomes a sustainable cash-flow engine.
questions.expert_context: Distinguish the user from the payer and separate actual payment from stated interest.

questions.prompt: What exactly does your solution do and which measurable customer outcome becomes better?
questions.why_it_matters: A solution must improve the customer outcome rather than merely add technology.
questions.expert_context: State the mechanism and the before-versus-after outcome without marketing language.

questions.prompt: What have you tested or achieved so far in usage pilots payments renewals retention or growth?
questions.why_it_matters: Stage-appropriate behavioural evidence tests whether the Horse can move.
questions.expert_context: Use consistent periods and definitions; pre-launch founders should describe the strongest completed validation experiment.

questions.prompt: How will you acquire serve and retain customers while producing sustainable cash flow?
questions.why_it_matters: Revenue that costs more to acquire or deliver than it creates is not an investable engine.
questions.expert_context: Explain price acquisition channel direct cost repeat behaviour and the most uncertain economic assumption.

questions.prompt: Why are you and your team unusually qualified to understand and solve this particular problem?
questions.why_it_matters: Founder–problem fit must come from relevant access capability or lived execution evidence.
questions.expert_context: Describe concrete experience relationships skills or insight; passion alone is not evidence.

questions.prompt: What difficult things have you built sold or operated and what did you change when evidence contradicted you?
questions.why_it_matters: Execution and learning velocity are more diagnostic than confidence.
questions.expert_context: Give one specific example showing ownership action feedback and a resulting change.

questions.prompt: What is the biggest unresolved risk and how will the team use its next period of time and capital to prove or disprove it?
questions.why_it_matters: Strong Jockeys identify the fatal unknown and buy evidence before scale.
questions.expert_context: Name the risk milestone time box budget success threshold and what you will do if the test fails.
